4 lemons: 2 cups sugar
Boil the sugar and water for 5 minutes.
Take off the heat, add the mint and steep for 15 minutes.
Strain and add the lemon juice.
Pour into a glass bottle.
Serve 1 part syrup with 4 parts cold water.
The syrup is concentrated; dilute before use.
The syrup keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge.
Apple and cinnamon compote
4 apples
4 cloves
6 cups water
Slice the apples.
Boil the water, sugar and spices.
Add the apples and cook for 10 minutes.
Leave to cool.
Resting the compote overnight intensifies the flavour.
Homemade quince compote
Peel and slice the quinces.
Boil the water, sugar and cinnamon.
Add the quinces and cook for 20 minutes.
Take off the heat once the quince is soft.
Chill and serve.
If you tie the quince seeds in muslin and cook them along, the colour turns pink.
Cocoa mosaic cake
2 packets petit beurre biscuits
Break the biscuits into large pieces by hand.
Heat and melt the milk, sugar, butter and cocoa; do not boil.
Once lukewarm, mix with the biscuits and walnuts.
Roll it up in cling film.
Chill for at least 4 hours and slice.
If you add the biscuits while the sauce is very hot, they turn doughy.
Serve with tea or coffee.
Wet cake (brownie style)
4 tablespoons cocoa
For the sauce: 1 cup milk, 2 tablespoons cocoa, 3 tablespoons sugar
Whisk the eggs and sugar until frothy; add the milk, oil and cocoa.
Sift in the flour and baking powder.
Bake in a greased square tin for 30 minutes.
Boil the sauce ingredients, pour over the hot cake and let cool.
Pour the sauce while the cake is hot; it soaks in well.
Lemon cake
Zest and juice of 1 lemon
2.5 cups flour
Preheat the oven to 175 °C.
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 4 minutes.
Add the lemon zest, juice, oil and yogurt.
Sift in the flour and baking powder and mix.
Bake in a greased tin for 40 minutes.
Yogurt keeps the cake moist.
Keeps for 3–4 days in an airtight container.
Marble cake
3 cups flour
Whisk the eggs and sugar until frothy and add the milk and oil.
Add the flour, baking powder and vanilla.
Mix cocoa into one third of the batter.
Pour plain and cocoa batter into the tin alternately, swirl with a toothpick and bake for 40 minutes.
If you mix too much, the pattern disappears.
Apple and cinnamon cookies
1 dessert spoon baking powder
For the filling: 2 grated apples, 2 tablespoons sugar, 1 dessert spoon cinnamon, half a cup walnuts
Cook the apples with sugar and cinnamon until the liquid is absorbed, then cool with the walnuts.
Beat the butter, icing sugar and egg, add the flour and make a dough.
Take pieces of dough, roll out, add the apple filling and close.
Bake at 180 °C for 20 minutes.
Dust with icing sugar once cool.
The filling must be completely cool so the dough doesn’t soften.
Melt-in-the-mouth shortbread cookies
250 g butter (room temperature)
1 cup icing sugar
About 3 cups flour
Half a cup cornflour
Beat the butter and icing sugar until creamy.
Add the vanilla, cornflour and flour gradually.
Roll the soft, non-sticky dough into walnut-sized balls.
Bake at 170 °C for 15 minutes so they stay pale.
The cookies shouldn’t change colour; that’s what gives the melt-in-the-mouth texture.
1 week in a closed tin.
Savoury cookies (with sesame)
About 3.5 cups flour
For the top: 1 dessert spoon sesame and 1 dessert spoon nigella seeds
Mix the butter, oil, yogurt, egg white and salt.
Add the baking powder and flour and knead a soft dough.
Shape the dough into sticks or rounds.
Brush with egg yolk and sprinkle with sesame.
Don’t overwork the dough.
Orange muffins
Zest and juice of 1 orange
Preheat the oven to 180 °C and line a muffin tin with cases.
Whisk the eggs and sugar.
Add the orange zest, juice, oil and yogurt.
Add the flour and baking powder and stir just until combined.
Fill the cases two-thirds full and bake for 22 minutes.
Don’t overmix muffin batter or it forms tunnels inside.
Chocolate chip cookies
Half a cup brown sugar
Half a cup granulated sugar
Half a teaspoon bicarbonate of soda
1 cup chocolate chips
Beat the butter and sugars, then add the egg and vanilla.
Mix the flour and bicarbonate of soda and add.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Rest the dough in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Make walnut-sized balls, space them apart and bake at 180 °C for 12 minutes.
Take them out while the centres still look soft; they firm up on the tray.
Banana walnut bread (banana bread)
3 very ripe bananas
Half a cup melted butter
1 dessert spoon bicarbonate of soda
Preheat the oven to 175 °C and grease a loaf tin.
Mash the bananas and mix with the eggs, sugar and butter.
Add the flour, bicarbonate of soda and cinnamon.
Fold in the walnuts.
Bake in the tin for 50 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Bananas with blackened skins give the sweetest result.
3 days in an airtight container; can be frozen.
Oat and peanut butter cookies
Half a cup peanut butter
Mix the peanut butter, egg and sugar.
